column1: # The host-path table of `just affected --narrow` (tools/recipes.py, the section above narrow()).
# glob<TAB>recipes<TAB>why[<TAB>exceptions]. A changed file that some gate reads through a dependency edge (a lib a target links,
# a manifest, a cargo global) selects the recipes of every row whose glob matches it; `*` keeps the full list; no row: the file's
# own derivation (the gates `python3 tools/recipes.py reach FILE` prints), and a file the derivation cannot read (not Rust source,
# deleted, a build script, in no lib's module tree, reached by no gate) keeps the full list and names the file and why. A file's
# own target (its bin, its test file, its lib's own tests), a script a recipe names, and the recipe's own text select their
# recipes without a row, so a row names only the gates that reach the file through a dependency; gate-ptx-spill joins a
# narrowed list only when a scan pair is not identical or its own inputs moved (tools/recipes.py, narrow()). `**` crosses
# A Rust file of a workspace crate whose diff is comments or layout only (equal tokens once both are left out) selects nothing, whatever row
# maps it (tools/recipes.py, CommentReads); an include macro that names it, a doc comment in a crate whose doctests a gate runs and the
# The recipes column is `*`, gate and weekly names, or `derive [gate-… …] [weekly-… …]`. `derive` stands for the gates the tree derives
# for the row, which this file does not hold: every gate whose own target names the module the glob stands for, and every gate the
# derivation says reaches a file the glob matches through another lib, less the row's exceptions (`python3 tools/recipes.py reach FILE…`
# prints those gates, each with one chain; `python3 tools/recipes.py rows` prints this table with them written out). A gate named
# beside `derive` is a hand extra: it links a file of the glob and the derivation does not reach it. A new gate or a new edge needs no
# edit here; a new row (glob, `derive`, why) is for bounding the next change to a new module. `just check-recipes` holds each row to the
# tree: its recipes are gate recipes that link every file it matches, each alternative matches a file, a row without `derive` has every
# gate the derivation names in it or in its exceptions, and a `derive` row the tree derives no gate for is red. The derivation reads
# the item graph of the code (use trees, paths, impls, macros; not docs) from each gate target's own items. The fourth
# column names the gates it reaches that a run-time dispatch keeps off the file: `except gate-… gate-…: reason`
# clauses joined by ` | ` (a serve seat the gate does not open, an Arch arm, a reference-set family it does not read);
# the check counts them in its summary, and an exception naming a gate that does not reach the file is red.
# A data file is read like the items around it: what a target takes by `include_str!`/`include_bytes!` or a path literal
# is a file it reaches, as its own target's (a test's data directory: picked without a row) or through a lib's code (a row,
# as for source). A row whose files only own targets read maps nothing, and the check takes it out.
# Every binary parses the registry and runs at_main first, and a lever's default reaches whoever reads it in place.
